target_customer: Online sellers, subscription businesses and their accountants and bookkeepers
problem: Sales, fees, refunds, payouts and taxes from many payment processors and sales channels must be reconciled by hand into accounting ledgers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for sync and reconciliation (Synder Sync) plus revenue recognition (Synder RevRec, launched 2024)

founders.name: Michael Astreiko
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he started in ecommerce then spent about seven years in fintech on online sales, accounting, bookkeeping and automation. He said in a podcast he is not an accountant. Education not found.

founders.name: Ilya Kisel
founders.background_notes: Named as COO and co-founder in the June 2021 press release and a TechCrunch image caption; the YC page lists only Astreiko.

competitors.name: A2X
competitors.what: Ecommerce accounting that reconciles Amazon and Shopify payouts to QuickBooks and Xero
competitors.traction_then: Launched A2X for Shopify in New Zealand in May 2019; a review site says it was purpose-built for ecommerce accounting since 2015 (unverified)

technical_complexity.rationale: Many marketplace, payment and ledger APIs must be matched and kept in sync with fee, refund and tax edge cases; the company reports about 1 billion dollars of 2020 transaction volume, so correctness at scale mattered.

defensibility.rationale: Integration breadth and historical ledger entries create some stickiness, but several rivals offered similar sync and the accounting platforms could extend their own apps.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or acquiring Synder; it reached Intuit platinum partner status in October 2025 per its news page.

market_need_then: Ecommerce growth and many payment processors made manual reconciliation painful; the company said it processed about 1 billion dollars of 2020 volume for several thousand companies (own press release, unverified).

branding.name_origin: The company blog says it wanted a name reflective of the product's abilities in a superhero-themed post; no literal meaning is stated.
branding.domain_note: Operates on synder.com, the exact .com; history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and benefit-focused with the slogan Machine accuracy. Human approach.

branding.community_and_virality: Company reports a 4.7 average rating from more than 3,400 reviews; its blog notes searches for the name can surface unrelated Snyder results.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong review volume on app marketplaces but the name is easily confused with Snyder and no mascot, merch or brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Synder, run by CloudBusiness Inc., was already selling to several thousand ecommerce companies before YC Summer 2021, raised a 2 million dollar late seed in June 2021 and added revenue recognition in 2024 and NetSuite and AI features in 2025. It is Active with no later priced round found and says it serves thousands of businesses with strong marketplace reviews. It grew from a crowded niche with a modest raise, suggesting capital efficiency, but no Series A appears.
notes: Founding year conflicts: YC says 2020, the press release says 2019, TechCrunch snippet says 2018 start with full time a year later, site structured data says 2014, another source says CloudBusiness in 2016. Seed of 2M stated by the press release (June 15, 2021) and a TechCrunch headline (August 27, 2021, not opened); a separate 1M seed in August 2021 and a 3M total are aggregator only. The 2020 Smart Partnership Capital angel is stated without an amount. Competitors Webgility, MyWorks Sync and Bookkeep are named only in 2025 era pages and so are excluded; A2X was sourced via a May 2019 press story.
